phrases: Every hair on your body has a tiny muscle attached to it.
When you're cold, scared, or you hear an amazing song,
your nerves tell those muscles to pull.
The hairs stand up, and the skin bumps up around them.
For animals with thick fur, that makes a fluffy coat that traps warm air.
And a scared cat puffs up, to look bigger.
But we lost most of our fur.
So for us, goosebumps are mostly a leftover from our hairy ancestors.
